name: Apollo 11 (Tranquility Base)

name: Apollo 12 (Intrepid)
note: Lander position from LROC (Wagner et al. 2017 / LROC anthropogenic-objects shapefile; coord source: Averaged Mapping Orbit NACs; uncertainty ~2.2 m; arrival 1969-11-19). Lunar Module descent stage.

name: Apollo 14 (Antares)
note: Lander position from LROC (Wagner et al. 2017 / LROC anthropogenic-objects shapefile; coord source: Averaged Mapping Orbit NACs + Laser Ranging; uncertainty ~0.4 m; arrival 1971-02-05). Lunar Module descent stage.

name: Apollo 15 (Falcon)
note: Lander position from LROC (Wagner et al. 2017 / LROC anthropogenic-objects shapefile; coord source: Averaged Mapping Orbit NACs + Laser Ranging; uncertainty ~1.0 m; arrival 1971-07-30). Lunar Module descent stage.

name: Apollo 16 (Orion)
note: Lander position from LROC (Wagner et al. 2017 / LROC anthropogenic-objects shapefile; coord source: Averaged Mapping Orbit NACs; uncertainty ~3.0 m; arrival 1972-04-21). Lunar Module descent stage.

name: Apollo 17 (Challenger)
note: Lander position from LROC (Wagner et al. 2017 / LROC anthropogenic-objects shapefile; coord source: Averaged Mapping Orbit NACs; uncertainty ~3.5 m; arrival 1972-12-11). Lunar Module descent stage.

name: Luna 16
note: Lander position from LROC (Wagner et al. 2017 / LROC anthropogenic-objects shapefile; coord source: Averaged Mapping Orbit NACs; uncertainty ~3.7 m; arrival 1970-09-12). Sample-return lander (Mare Fecunditatis).

name: Luna 17 (Lunokhod 1 lander)
note: Lander position from LROC (Wagner et al. 2017 / LROC anthropogenic-objects shapefile; coord source: Averaged Mapping Orbit NACs + Laser Ranging; uncertainty ~0.5 m; arrival 1970-11-10). Lunokhod 1 rover later drove to ~38.315N, -35.008E (laser-ranged retroreflector).

name: Luna 21 (Lunokhod 2 lander)
note: Lander position from LROC (Wagner et al. 2017 / LROC anthropogenic-objects shapefile; coord source: Averaged NACs; uncertainty ~13.4 m; arrival 1973-01-08). Le Monnier crater region; low-precision position (+/-13 m).

name: Luna 24
note: Lander position from LROC (Wagner et al. 2017 / LROC anthropogenic-objects shapefile; coord source: Averaged Mapping Orbit NACs; uncertainty ~3.7 m; arrival 1976-08-09). Sample-return lander (Mare Crisium); Luna 23 landed ~5 km away.

name: Luna 25 impact site
note: Lander position from LROC (Wagner et al. 2017 / LROC anthropogenic-objects shapefile; coord source: Averaged NACs; uncertainty ~18.5 m; arrival 2023-08-19). Crashed 2023-08-19 during a failed orbit-lowering maneuver; not a soft landing. Position uncertainty ~18.5 m.

name: Luna 9
note: First soft landing (1966-02-03 18:45:30 UTC). Historical/nominal position 7 deg 08' N, 64 deg 22' W; NOT LROC-measured, uncertain by kilometres. A 2026 paper proposed 7.03N, 64.33W as the probable true site.

name: Surveyor 1
note: Lander position from LROC (Wagner et al. 2017 / LROC anthropogenic-objects shapefile; coord source: Averaged NACs; uncertainty ~5.4 m; arrival 1966-05-30).

name: Surveyor 3
note: Lander position from LROC (Wagner et al. 2017 / LROC anthropogenic-objects shapefile; coord source: Averaged Mapping Orbit NACs; uncertainty ~2.6 m; arrival 1967-04-20). Apollo 12 landed ~160 m away.

name: Surveyor 7
note: Lander position from LROC (Wagner et al. 2017 / LROC anthropogenic-objects shapefile; coord source: Averaged Mapping Orbit NACs; uncertainty ~2.7 m; arrival 1968-01-10). Tycho ejecta blanket.

name: Chang'e 3 (Yutu 1)
note: Lander position from LROC (Wagner et al. 2017 / LROC anthropogenic-objects shapefile; coord source: Averaged NACs; uncertainty ~9.1 m; arrival 2013-12-14). Mare Imbrium (Sinus Iridum region).

name: Chang'e 4 (Yutu 2)
note: Lander position from LROC (Wagner et al. 2017 / LROC anthropogenic-objects shapefile; coord source: NAC DTM; uncertainty ~10.0 m; arrival 2019-01-03). First far-side landing; Von Karman crater, South Pole-Aitken basin.

name: Chang'e 5
note: Lander position from LROC (Wagner et al. 2017 / LROC anthropogenic-objects shapefile; coord source: NAC DTM; uncertainty ~10.0 m; arrival 2020-12-01). Sample return; northern Oceanus Procellarum near Mons Rumker.

name: Chang'e 6
note: Lander position from LROC (Wagner et al. 2017 / LROC anthropogenic-objects shapefile; coord source: NAC DTM; uncertainty ~10.0 m; arrival 2024-06-01). Far-side sample return; Apollo basin in South Pole-Aitken.

name: Chang'e 7 (planned, Shackleton rim)
note: Planned south-pole landing on the illuminated rim of Shackleton crater (no official final site). Reported target 88 deg 48' S, 123 deg 24' E (Wikipedia) / 88.8S, 123.4E (China in Space); matches the 'Shackleton ridge point D' illumination site. Launch (set for ~Aug 23 2026) was scrubbed for weather; reports conflict on whether the new window is Sept 2026 or 2027, and no launch/landing was confirmed in sources reviewed as of 2026-11-14.

name: Chandrayaan-3 (Shiv Shakti point)
note: Lander position from LROC (Wagner et al. 2017 / LROC anthropogenic-objects shapefile; coord source: NAC DTM; uncertainty ~10.0 m; arrival 2023-08-23). Vikram lander touchdown 2023-08-23. Official name of the point: Shiv Shakti.

name: Chandrayaan-2 Vikram impact site
note: Lander position from LROC (Wagner et al. 2017 / LROC anthropogenic-objects shapefile; coord source: Averaged NACs; uncertainty ~9.1 m; arrival 2019-09-06). Crashed 2019-09-06 (failed soft landing).

name: SLIM
note: Lander position from LROC (Wagner et al. 2017 / LROC anthropogenic-objects shapefile; coord source: NAC DTM; uncertainty ~10.0 m; arrival 2024-01-19). Near Shioli crater; landed 2024-01-19, nose-down/on its side; survived 3 lunar nights.

name: IM-1 Odysseus
note: Lander position from LROC (Wagner et al. 2017 / LROC anthropogenic-objects shapefile; coord source: NAC DTM; uncertainty ~10.0 m; arrival 2024-02-22). Malapert A region; tipped over on a 12 deg slope. LROC image NAC M1463440322L.

name: IM-2 Athena
note: Lander position from LROC (Wagner et al. 2017 / LROC anthropogenic-objects shapefile; coord source: NAC DTM; uncertainty ~5.0 m; arrival 2025-03-06). Landed ~250 m from target near Mons Mouton, came to rest on its side in a crater; mission ended <13 h later.

name: Blue Ghost Mission 1
note: Lander position from LROC (Wagner et al. 2017 / LROC anthropogenic-objects shapefile; coord source: NAC DTM; uncertainty ~10.0 m; arrival 2025-03-02). Mare Crisium near Mons Latreille; full 14-day mission.

name: Hakuto-R Mission 2 (Resilience) impact site
note: Lander position from LROC (Wagner et al. 2017 / LROC anthropogenic-objects shapefile; coord source: NAC DTM; uncertainty ~10.0 m; arrival 2025-06-05). Crashed 2025-06-05 ~19:17 UTC during landing attempt (Mare Frigoris); not a soft landing.

name: IM-3 (planned, Reiner Gamma)
note: IM-3 'Trinity' targets the Reiner Gamma lunar swirl; exact aim point unpublished, so Reiner Gamma's centre (7 deg 30' N, 59 deg 00' W) is used. As of Sept 2026 NASA lists launch as early 2027.

name: Griffin-1 (planned, Nobile / Mons Mouton area)
note: Astrobotic Griffin Mission 1 (Falcon Heavy, planned NET Nov 2026) targets the mountainous area west of Nobile crater near Mons Mouton (the former VIPER site). No coordinates are published; the Mons Mouton summit (84 deg 36' S, 31 deg 00' E) is used as a representative point.

name: Peak near Cabeus B
note: Representative point = centre of Cabeus B crater (82.4S, 53.0W, Wikipedia); the actual peak is nearby (region described as ~200 km from the pole). LOW confidence in exact position. Region name per NASA (Oct 2024; reaffirmed in LPSC 2026 abstract 1901). NASA published no coordinates, only maps. NOTE: in Feb 2026 NASA changed Artemis III to a low-Earth-orbit docking test; the first crewed landing is now Artemis IV (early 2028), which is not limited to these regions.

name: Haworth
note: Representative point = Haworth crater centre (86 deg 54' S, 4 deg 00' W, Wikipedia); the candidate sites lie on the crater's rim/peak terrain. Region name per NASA (Oct 2024; reaffirmed in LPSC 2026 abstract 1901). NASA published no coordinates, only maps. NOTE: in Feb 2026 NASA changed Artemis III to a low-Earth-orbit docking test; the first crewed landing is now Artemis IV (early 2028), which is not limited to these regions.

name: Malapert Massif
note: Representative point = 86S, 0E, described by LROC as the heart of the Artemis candidate landing region on the Malapert massif. Mazarico/Bussey-type illumination points M1 (86.04S, 2.7E) and M2 (86.00S, 2.9W) bracket it. Region name per NASA (Oct 2024; reaffirmed in LPSC 2026 abstract 1901). NASA published no coordinates, only maps. NOTE: in Feb 2026 NASA changed Artemis III to a low-Earth-orbit docking test; the first crewed landing is now Artemis IV (early 2028), which is not limited to these regions.

name: Mons Mouton Plateau
note: Representative point = IM-2 Athena's LROC-measured landing position, which is on the Mons Mouton plateau (widest, flattest candidate area). Approximation of region centre. Region name per NASA (Oct 2024; reaffirmed in LPSC 2026 abstract 1901). NASA published no coordinates, only maps. NOTE: in Feb 2026 NASA changed Artemis III to a low-Earth-orbit docking test; the first crewed landing is now Artemis IV (early 2028), which is not limited to these regions.

name: Mons Mouton
note: Representative point = Mons Mouton highest point (84 deg 36' S, 31 deg 00' E, Wikipedia); formerly 'Leibnitz Beta'. Region name per NASA (Oct 2024; reaffirmed in LPSC 2026 abstract 1901). NASA published no coordinates, only maps. NOTE: in Feb 2026 NASA changed Artemis III to a low-Earth-orbit docking test; the first crewed landing is now Artemis IV (early 2028), which is not limited to these regions.

name: Nobile Rim 1
note: NASA describes Nobile Rim 1 as the SOUTHWEST rim of Nobile crater (Space.com/astronomy.com descriptions). Representative point DERIVED by us: the point diametrically opposite the published Nobile Rim 2 point through the crater centre (85.28S, 53.27E). Not a published coordinate; LOW confidence. Region name per NASA (Oct 2024; reaffirmed in LPSC 2026 abstract 1901). NASA published no coordinates, only maps. NOTE: in Feb 2026 NASA changed Artemis III to a low-Earth-orbit docking test; the first crewed landing is now Artemis IV (early 2028), which is not limited to these regions.

name: Nobile Rim 2
note: Representative point = top-ranked point 358 for 'Nobile Rim 2' (84.20156S, 60.69989E) from Table 3 of Evaluating potential landing sites for Artemis III (arXiv 2406.19863); region is the NE rim of Nobile. Region name per NASA (Oct 2024; reaffirmed in LPSC 2026 abstract 1901). NASA published no coordinates, only maps. NOTE: in Feb 2026 NASA changed Artemis III to a low-Earth-orbit docking test; the first crewed landing is now Artemis IV (early 2028), which is not limited to these regions.

name: de Gerlache Rim 2
note: Representative point = top-ranked point 726 for 'de Gerlache Rim 2' (88 deg 30' 56.38" S, 61 deg 10' 2.35" 'O') from Table 3 of arXiv 2406.19863; the paper prints 'O' for the hemisphere, interpreted as West (de Gerlache is at 87.1W). Medium-low confidence. Region name per NASA (Oct 2024; reaffirmed in LPSC 2026 abstract 1901). NASA published no coordinates, only maps. NOTE: in Feb 2026 NASA changed Artemis III to a low-Earth-orbit docking test; the first crewed landing is now Artemis IV (early 2028), which is not limited to these regions.

name: Slater Plain
note: Representative point = Slater crater centre (88 deg 05' S, 111 deg 17' E, Wikipedia); 'Slater Plain' is the low rolling terrain near it (lowest of the 9 regions, -1800 to -300 m). LOW confidence in exact position. Region name per NASA (Oct 2024; reaffirmed in LPSC 2026 abstract 1901). NASA published no coordinates, only maps. NOTE: in Feb 2026 NASA changed Artemis III to a low-Earth-orbit docking test; the first crewed landing is now Artemis IV (early 2028), which is not limited to these regions.

name: Shackleton ridge point A
note: 81% illuminated over 2020; min 44% / max 98% per lunar day. Exact provenance of each point is not given by Wikipedia; verify against the paper before quoting.
